title: Exit Through the Gift Shop: Reflection Lab
summary: A self-paced follow-up to Banksy's Exit Through the Gift Shop. Students investigate Mr. Brainwash, money laundering in the art market and NFTs, all through the question 'Can anyone be an artist?'
overview: Built as a 'work alone' lesson for after the class has watched the film. Five tabs take students through a film reflection, Mr. Brainwash's 2008 show 'Life is Beautiful', art as a value container for laundering and sanctions evasion (freeports, Basel Institute), and a quick recap of NFTs (the Beeple sale). Each tab gives curated sources, critical prompts and a small micro-task.

The final submission is a short-answer template, not an essay. It is built on the Knowledge Framework (scope, methods & tools, perspectives, ethics) plus 2–3 TOK concepts. Each answer has to cite a specific scene and two details from the sources, which makes generic AI answers easy to spot.
A separate last tab asks students to pitch a year-group art action after browsing HEART, the art museum in Herning. Swap in your own local museum, or skip it.
questions: Who has the authority to label something 'important' art?
How much of an artwork's value is belief, authority and scarcity rather than quality?
Is a documentary a source of knowledge, or an artwork in disguise?
time: One lesson, after the film (86 min)
needs: The film watched beforehand. It has strong language, so check the rating for your group.
heads_up: The HEART / class-trip tab and a couple of lines in the intro are specific to our school. Edit them or tell students to skip that tab.
